title: Embeddings: meaning as numbers
blurb: How text becomes numbers that capture what it means.

slides.title: Turning meaning into numbers
body: An embedding is a list of numbers that represents a piece of text — a word, a sentence or a whole document.
It’s produced by a model trained so that texts with similar meanings get similar numbers. The individual numbers don’t mean much on their own; the pattern does.

visual.caption: Numbers made up for illustration. Real embeddings have hundreds or thousands of numbers each.

slides.title: Close together means similar
body: Think of each embedding as a point on a map with many dimensions. Texts with similar meanings land near each other.
That works even when they share no words at all — it’s the meaning that matters, not the spelling.

visual.caption: Closeness is measured mathematically, by comparing the two lists of numbers.
visual.question: Which is closest to “How do I reset my password?”

slides.title: Search by meaning, not keywords
body: Keyword search finds documents that contain your words. Semantic search finds documents that mean what you meant.

visual.caption: Documents are embedded once. Each question only needs one new embedding.

items.label: 1. Embed your documents
items.text: Each document, or chunk of one, becomes a list of numbers, stored in a database.

items.label: 2. Embed the question
items.text: The search query becomes a list of numbers too.

items.label: 3. Find the nearest
items.text: Return the documents whose embeddings are closest to the question’s.

slides.title: Where embeddings are used
body: Embeddings are a building block behind many AI features — often ones you don’t notice.
The next lesson looks at the most important one for chatbots.

visual.caption: All of these rely on “close together means similar”.

items.heading: Semantic search
items.text: Finding help articles that answer the question, whatever words were used.

items.heading: Recommendations
items.text: “More like this” for articles, products or support tickets.

items.heading: Grouping and duplicates
items.text: Clustering feedback by theme, or spotting near-identical records.

items.heading: Retrieval for chatbots
items.text: Finding the right documents to give a model before it answers.

quiz.question: What is an embedding?
options: A list of numbers that represents the meaning of a piece of text
A picture inserted into a document
The model’s reply to a question
quiz.explanation: Embeddings turn text into numbers arranged so that similar meanings end up close together.

quiz.question: Why can semantic search match “I forgot my login” with “How do I reset my password?”
options: Their embeddings are close because their meanings are similar
They were written by the same person
quiz.explanation: The two share almost no words, but their meanings are close — and embeddings capture meaning.

quiz.question: Which task suits embeddings best?
options: Finding support articles similar to a customer’s question
quiz.explanation: Embeddings are designed for comparing meaning, so “find things like this” tasks are their strength.
